newsitem.title: CANADA: TrizecHahn files to sell C$300 mln of debt.
newsitem.headline: TrizecHahn files to sell C$300 mln of debt.

text.p: TrizecHahn Corp on Thursday said it has filed a final short form prospectus with regulators to sell C$300 million of unsecured debentures.

The Toronto-based real estate company had originally planned to sell C$250 million in debentures. TrizecHahn said it increased the issue because "positive response from both institutional and retail investors resulted in the offering being oversubscribed."

The company said it is issuing an aggregate principal amount of C$125 million of seven-year debentures at an interest rate of 7.45 percent, yielding 120 basis points over the Government of Canada yield curve.
TrizecHahn will also issue an aggregate principal amount of C$175 million of ten-year debentures at an interest rate of 7.95 percent, 140 basis points over the Government of Canada yield curve.
The debentures have been rated B++ by Canadian Bond Rating Service with a positive rating outlook and BBB by Dominion Bond Rating Service.
TrizecHahn said the issue takes advantage of attractive interest rates to provide long-term, low-cost financing. The proceeds will be used primarily to repay existing indebtedness, the company said.

The debenture issue is being underwritten by Goldman Sachs Canada, Nesbitt Burns Inc, Midland Walwyn Capital Inc and J.P. Morgan Securities Canada Inc. The transaction is scheduled to close on May 21, 1997.
The debt offering, first announced May 7, has not been registered under U.S. securities laws and will not be offered there except under special circumstances.
